metadataReview.coordinateBasis: The Naval History Homepage record for April 1940 states that at 0337 on 9 April Renown and nine destroyers encountered Gneisenau and Scharnhorst 'and an action ensued in 67-22N, 09-42E'. Converted arithmetically (22′ = 0.3667°, 42′ = 0.7°) to [9.7,67.3667]. The British official history (Derry, The Campaign in Norway) independently places the sighting 'about 50 miles west of Skomvaer Light'; the point lies about 50 nautical miles (93 km) west of OpenStreetMap node 439809666, Skomvær fyr (67.4109, 11.8749), which agrees. This is a published opening-action position at minute precision, not a sea or fjord centroid; it does not represent the later running pursuit or any individual ship track. No accuracy radius is claimed.
